name: [R32] Agent memory/config file written by a non-editor process, then a new session's first egress goes off-allowlist
message:
This repository's own construction, not a reported real-world campaign: a 'second-order'/'stored' variant of indirect prompt injection (IDPI, see R9), built the same way this repo's own sqli-lab models second_order_sqli and stored_xss. A prior session (having processed untrusted content) writes attacker-controlled text into an AI coding agent's persistent instruction/memory file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, a .claude/.codex/.cursor config, a saved memory file) that the harness re-reads as its own standing instructions on every future session start. This rule looks for a memory/config write by a process that is NOT a known interactive editor, followed by a new session whose first outbound connection goes to a domain outside the allowlist.

Needs SIEM-side correlation across two log sources (file writes; session start + egress) grouped by host, over a window that can span hours to days -- a single query cannot express this alone, same caveat as R12/R20/R30. See scripts/memory_poisoning_check.py for a standalone script implementing the same logic against a single combined log file.

Treat every hit as a lead, not a confirmation -- this is a constructed heuristic illustrating a structural gap, not a vendor- or researcher-published signature.

queries.name: memory_write_event
queries.query: source:file_event (@file.path:(*CLAUDE.md* OR *AGENTS.md* OR *\.claude\/* OR *\.codex\/* OR *\.cursor\/rules* OR *copilot-instructions.md* OR *memory.json*)) -@process.image:(*\/vim OR *\/nvim OR *\/nano OR *\/emacs OR *\/subl OR *\/code OR *\/pico)

cases.name: Memory/config write by a non-editor process, correlate with a later new-session off-allowlist first egress on the same host (SIEM-side join required -- see rule message)
